notes: NO official ktu.edu.in direct PDF URL for a 2024-scheme course syllabus could be confirmed. ktu.edu.in / www.ktu.edu.in serve the Academics area as a client-rendered SPA; /academics/scheme, /academics/branchsyllabus, /academics/branchcurriculum/hardcoded-btech and /academics/view-questionpapers all return only site chrome when fetched, with no syllabus anchors. The apex host ktu.edu.in also fails TLS (ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID); only www.ktu.edu.in resolves.

A URL published by search engines, https://ktu.edu.in/data/Syllabus for S1 and S2_KTU.pdf, was tested and does NOT serve a PDF (it returns the SPA HTML shell), so it is recorded here as unverified/not a working syllabus link.

sourceUrl for each course is an unofficial third-party mirror (ktu.notesundo.in), because no official per-course PDF URL was reachable. Every mirror PDF is an unmodified KTU document: each carries the running header 'B.Tech 2024 -S1/S2' (S1 courses) and footer 'APJ Abdul Kalam Technological University', and each reproduces KTU's own 'Course Assessment Method (CIE: 40 marks, ESE: 60 marks)' block.

Topic strings are verbatim phrases lifted from the module paragraph in the source PDF. KTU writes each module as one dense paragraph separated by semicolons and CAPITALISED lead-ins; the array here is that same text split at those separators. No topic text was rewritten.
CO statements and Bloom's codes are verbatim from the source PDF's Course Outcomes table. KTU codes this column 'Bloom's Knowledge Level (KL)'.
Module 'hours' are the 'Contact Hours' column of the source PDF. They are per-module contact hours, not the L/T/P/R teaching hours.

examPattern is taken from the 'End Semester Examination Marks (ESE)' block inside each syllabus PDF. UCHUT346 is an HMC course and therefore has a DIFFERENT pattern (50 marks, 6x3 Part A, 4x8 Part B) - do not assume the 60-mark pattern for every course.

durationHours 2.5 = 'Exam Hours 2 Hrs. 30 Min.' as printed in every syllabus header observed. The Academic Regulations 2024 do not themselves fix an ESE duration; they only fix the 2-hour internal written examination (R 7.5).

Not verified: lab/practical courses, seminars, projects and Level 5 elective courses were not retrieved as syllabus documents, so no examPattern variant for those is asserted. The 2019->2024 comparison claims circulating on non-official sites (for example 'Python replaced C in S1') are not reproduced here because the official 2024 curriculum shows BOTH 'Algorithmic Thinking with Python' (UCEST105, S1) and 'Programming in C' (GXEST204, S2) as separate courses.

Two official KTU documents disagree on the course-category credit split for 2024: the Academic Regulations 2024 R 3.15 gives PCC 52 and PWS 12, while the B.Tech Curriculum 2024 gives PCC 54 and PWS 10 (both total 167 academic credits). This is an inconsistency in the sources, not a transcription error here.

PCECT302 is indexed under the mirror's slug 'solid-state-devices' but the PDF asset is named 'Analog-Circuits-PCECT302'. The PDF's own heading is 'SEMESTER S3 SOLID STATE DEVICES', which is what is recorded here.
The 6 courses below are all courses for which a real module list AND a real CO table were retrieved. They are a seed index, not the full 2024 course catalogue.

courses.title: Algorithmic Thinking with Python

topics: PROBLEM-SOLVING STRATEGIES
Problem-solving strategies defined
Importance of understanding multiple problem-solving strategies
Trial and Error
Heuristics
Means-Ends Analysis
Backtracking (Working backward)
THE PROBLEM-SOLVING PROCESS
Computer as a model of computation
Understanding the problem
Formulating a model
Developing an algorithm
Writing the program
Testing the program
Evaluating the solution
ESSENTIALS OF PYTHON PROGRAMMING
Creating and using variables in Python
Numeric and String data types in Python
Using the math module
Using the Python Standard Library for handling basic I/O - print, input

modules.title: Algorithm and Pseudocode Representation; Flowcharts

Symbols used in creating a Flowchart - start and end, arithmetic calculations, input/output operation, decision (selection), module name (call), for loop (Hexagon), flow-lines, on-page connector, off-page connector

DECOMPOSITION AND MODULARIZATION
Problem decomposition as a strategy for solving complex problems
Modularization

Defining and using functions in Python
Functions with multiple return values
RECURSION
Recursion Defined
Reasons for using Recursion
The Call Stack
Recursion and the Stack
Avoiding Circularity in Recursion

Sample problems - Finding the nth Fibonacci number, greatest common divisor of two positive integers, the factorial of a positive integer, adding two positive integers, the sum of digits of a positive number

modules.title: Computational Approaches to Problem-Solving
topics: Brute-force Approach - Example: Padlock, Password guessing
Divide-and-conquer Approach - Example: The Merge Sort Algorithm
Advantages of Divide and Conquer Approach
Disadvantages of Divide and Conquer Approach
Dynamic Programming Approach - Example: Fibonacci series

Motivations for the Greedy Approach
Characteristics of the Greedy Algorithm
Greedy Algorithms vs Dynamic Programming
Randomized Approach - Example 1: coupon collector (jeans coupons); Example 2: hat-check problem
Motivations for the Randomized Approach
Introductory diagrammatic/algorithmic explanations only; Analysis not required
